fact.text: A group of flamingos is called a flamboyance, a name that fits a crowd of bright pink birds standing on one leg.

heads_up: Savaitgalį vietomis gali susidaryti plikledis – vairuotojams ir pėstiesiems verta saugotis.

lithuania.headline: Kariuomenės vadas siūlo fizinius barjerus pasienyje su Kaliningradu
lithuania.summary: Kariuomenės vadas gen. Raimundas Vaikšnoras siūlo pažeidžiamose pasienio su Kaliningrado sritimi vietose įrengti fizinius barjerus, panašius į tvorą su Baltarusija, nes nuolatinis karių patruliavimas brangus ir atitraukia nuo pratybų. Sustiprinta apsauga, kurioje dalyvauja apie 100 karių, pratęsta iki lapkričio pabaigos.
lithuania.context: Nuo 2022 m. Rusijos invazijos į Ukrainą Lietuva stiprina sienas: pasienyje su Baltarusija pastatyta tvora. Spalio 8 d. kariai pradėjo padėti pasieniečiams prie Kaliningrado, reaguojant į pranešimus apie galimą Rusijos mobilizaciją, nors pareigūnai sako, kad grėsmė nepadidėjo.

lithuania.headline: Streikuoja apie 4 tūkst. mokytojų, ministrė sako, kad pinigų nėra
lithuania.summary: Neterminuotame streike dalyvauja apie 4 tūkst. pedagogų iš 220 mokyklų; jie reikalauja bent 10 proc. didesnių algų koeficientų, tam reikėtų 78,5 mln. eurų. Švietimo ministrė Raminta Popovienė, trečiadienį susitinkanti su streikuojančiais Nemenčinėje, sako, kad biudžete lėšų nėra – planuojamas 7,56 proc. algų augimas.
lithuania.context: Lietuvos švietimo darbuotojų profesinė sąjunga neterminuotą streiką pradėjo pirmadienį, nesutarusi su Vyriausybe dėl algų kitų metų biudžete. Profsąjunga siekia, kad mokytojų vidutinis atlyginimas artėtų prie 130 proc. šalies vidurkio.

lithuania.headline: Koalicijoje – ginčai dėl biudžeto ir šeimos referendumo
lithuania.summary: Demokratų lyderis Virginijus Sinkevičius „politiniu šantažu“ vadina „valstiečių“ grasinimą nepalaikyti kitų metų biudžeto, jei Seime nepajudės referendumas dėl šeimos sampratos, ir reikalauja biudžete spręsti paramos šeimoms bei statutinių pareigūnų algų klausimus.
lithuania.context: Valdančiąją koaliciją sudaro socialdemokratai, demokratai „Vardan Lietuvos“ ir „valstiečiai“. „Valstiečiai“ siekia patariamojo referendumo per 2027 m. savivaldos rinkimus, ar Konstitucijoje įtvirtinti, kad šeima kyla tik iš vyro ir moters santuokos; biudžetas Seime netrukus bus svarstomas pirmą kartą.

world.headline: Xi and Putin open talks in Shenzhen before meeting Trump
world.summary: Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin began talks at the Apec summit in Shenzhen, a day before a three-way meeting with Donald Trump that Putin expects to be 'highly useful'; Putin told the summit Western sanctions had 'failed'.
world.context: Trump flew in from Manila after an Asean summit; the trilateral meeting is due to include nuclear talks.

world.headline: Democrat Peltola wins Alaska, giving party 56 Senate seats
world.summary: Mary Peltola beat Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan after two weeks of counting, the last Senate race to be called; Democrats flipped nine seats, the most since 1958, and turn a 53-47 Republican majority into 56-44 for them.
world.context: The midterm elections were held on 3 November and gave Democrats both houses of Congress. Peltola's race was clouded by claims her aides recruited a second, unknown 'Dan Sullivan' to confuse voters, which she denies.

world.headline: Rubio says US tech outages are not linked or malicious
world.summary: Speaking in Manila, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said there is 'zero evidence' that a string of outages, which hit flights, banks, Microsoft and Apple, are linked to each other, to cyberattacks or to foreign states.
world.context: In recent days a glitch briefly grounded all US flights, Microsoft Outlook was down for nearly a day and major banks and Apple services failed.

world.headline: Netanyahu's opponents elect new Knesset speaker
world.summary: Israel's parliament elected Matan Kahana, an ally of Gadi Eisenkot, as speaker with 66 of 120 votes, backed by opposition and Arab-led parties, against 52 for Netanyahu's candidate.
world.context: Netanyahu's camp lost its majority in the 27 October election, and Eisenkot, a former army chief, has up to five more weeks to form a government. His bloc wants to set term limits for prime ministers and reverse laws limiting the courts.

interesting.headline: GTA 6 leads Game Awards nominations before it is even out
interesting.summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 got eight nominations, including Game of the Year against 007 First Light, Control Resonant, Phantom Blade Zero, Resident Evil Requiem and Zelda: Ocarina of Time, two days before Thursday's launch; it is estimated to have made about $1.5bn in pre-launch sales.
interesting.context: It is Rockstar's first new GTA in 13 years; winners are named on 10 December.

interesting.headline: Waymo pulls robotaxis from all US freeways
interesting.summary: Waymo halted freeway rides in all 15 US cities it serves after California's DMV called its freeway driving an 'imminent hazard' when its robotaxis repeatedly drove into active construction zones; city-street rides continue.
interesting.context: Waymo is Alphabet's driverless taxi company.

interesting.headline: Amazon and Google to own nearly 30% of Anthropic after IPO
interesting.summary: Anthropic's IPO filings show Amazon will own 14.7% and Google 13.7% after the listing, and a group of tech firms including Google, Nvidia and Microsoft will buy $26bn of non-voting shares.
interesting.context: Anthropic is the AI company that makes the Claude chatbot.

interesting.headline: Žalgiris beat Bayern 117-114 in record-scoring game
interesting.summary: Žalgiris beat Bayern Munich 117-114 after overtime in their highest-scoring Euroleague game ever, extending their winning run to six.

events.title: EU-UK summit expected to seal youth mobility deal

ongoing.title: Russia-Ukraine war
ongoing.update: A span of the Kerch bridge to Crimea collapsed into the sea after what Zelensky called a seven-stage drone and missile operation; the Kremlin vowed to rebuild it. The US told Kyiv's backers deep strikes don't work, which Germany's minister called 'stupid'.
ongoing.context: Russia seized Crimea in 2014 and launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Ukraine pushed Russian troops back from Kyiv that year, but the front has since largely stalled. Both sides now strike each other's infrastructure far behind the lines while the US pushes for peace talks.

ongoing.title: US-Iran tensions
ongoing.update: Hours after a US strike on Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, Iran attacked Kuwait and Bahrain, ending a two-month lull in its strikes on US targets.
ongoing.context: A war began in late February 2026 when the US and Israel struck Iran. Fighting eased after that, but the two sides keep clashing over the Strait of Hormuz, a key route for the world's oil, where tankers have been hit by mines.

ongoing.title: Nvidia CEO's affair with alleged Chinese spy
ongoing.update: Nvidia's board ruled out bringing Jensen Huang back as sales doubled to $115.8bn and it forecast $130bn next quarter; it also stopped shipping Hopper chips to China. The SEC is reportedly investigating, and Huang will testify to Congress on 1 December.
ongoing.context: Jensen Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and led it to become the world's most valuable chipmaker during the AI boom. Earlier this month he resigned after admitting an affair with a woman suspected of spying for China. He has since said he would be honoured to return, and Trump has backed the idea.
